messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2026-9876 — service=redwood-gpu-infer-west2a, symptom=CUDA_ALLOC_RETRY_FAIL (rate 82/min). auto-threshold triggered: 5m window > 30 errs.

pagerduty-bot: Pager assigned to @Ria Patel (on-call) — please acknowledge within 2m. Priority: P1.

Ria Patel: acked. I'm on it. pinging logs and recent deploys.

Omar Lee: saw this pop up on our dashboards — kvcache eviction spiking right before alloc failures. Noticed a noisy customer ramp on model=redwood-13b-quant.

Jia Chen: starting a quick runbook check: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/gpu-alloc-failure . First step: check node pressure + pod events, then consider fallback routing.

Ria Patel: running kubectl -n inference describe pod infer-west2a-3f9b | tail -n 40 to get OOM logs.

Ria Patel: ```Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x3 over 5m)  default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient memory, 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
  Warning  OutOfMemory     1m (x12 over 4m) kubelet               Pod was OOMKilled
Logs show repeated cudaMalloc retries then 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: out of memory'.
```

Santiago Ruiz: confirm which customers are on that pool — routing table shows customers: acme-marketing-prod, glanceai-indexer (staging), and tenant-phi-analytics. Might be 2 live prod customers.

CS-ops: acme-marketing-prod reported slow responses ~10:12. They flagged increased 500s on inference endpoint. Notified their CSM.

Omar Lee: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily enable model-fallback for that pool -> route new requests to redwood-13b-quant-fallback in behind-the-scenes group; 2) trigger kv-cache aggressive eviction on affected nodes; 3) cordon + restart one hot pod to clear CUDA state.

Jia Chen: executing fallback toggle: ``/api/route/update?pool=infer-west2a&fallback=true`` -> response 200. Starting to flip routing now.

incident-bot: Auto-check: fallback route activation acknowledged by controller (txn=0x7b2c). Monitoring for error rate delta.

Ria Patel: applying eviction policy patch to daemonset: ``kubectl -n infra patch ds kv-evictor --patch '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"evictor","env":[{"name":"EVICT_THRESHOLD","value":"0.6"}] }]}}}}'`` — rolled to 3/3 nodes.

Santiago Ruiz: I'm starting a rolling restart on pod infer-west2a-3f9b: ``kubectl rollout restart deploy/infer-node-west2a``. Restarting 1 pod at a time.

Omar Lee: monitoring: CUDA_ALLOC errors dropped from 82/min -> 9/min within 45s after fallback. Latency for acme-marketing-prod improved to baseline ~120ms.

Ria Patel: good. marking incident as mitigated for immediate customer impact but keeping page open for root cause. Will run heap/proc scans and collect coredumps.

Jia Chen: collecting diagnostics: nvprof traces and /var/log/nvidia-installer logs. Saving to s3://redwood-diagnostics/INC-2026-9876/ .

CS-ops: inbound CS update sent to acme contact: "We've routed your traffic to a compatible fallback model to restore latency. We're investigating the root cause and will follow up with timeline."

Santiago Ruiz: next steps: 1) analyze kvcache fragmentation and recent config bump (we shipped kvcache retention change yesterday at 03:00 UTC); 2) validate model memory footprint — regression test new quantization on dev; 3) plan hotfix if we confirm regression.

Ria Patel: preparing handoff to next oncall @Omar in 30m with notes and required follow-ups. If errors creep back above 30/min, auto-page will escalate to SRE lead.

Omar Lee: acked handoff plan. I'll own triage for the next 2h and follow the post-incident checklist. Dropping a summary to #incidents after root cause analysis.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note — INC-2026-9876 acknowledged by Ria Patel at 1759001250, status=acknowledged.

Ria Patel: closing this notification thread (keeping incident open). Will attach coredumps and timeline shortly. :white_check_mark:
